nodes.label: Two-Project Vercel Architecture (saarthi-mail + saarthi-mail-api)
nodes.rationale: Frontend and backend deploy as two separate Vercel projects on default *.vercel.app subdomains so no custom domain is required; frontend is a static Vite dist build, backend is a serverless function. Custom domains later require only env var and Google Console updates, no code changes.

nodes.label: MongoDB-Backed Session Store (connect-mongo)
nodes.rationale: Vercel serverless functions have no sticky sessions and no in-memory state across cold starts, so Express sessions must be persisted in MongoDB Atlas via connect-mongo. Without it every post-login request 401s.

nodes.label: Trust Proxy and Secure Cookies Behind Vercel
nodes.rationale: app.set("trust proxy", 1) is required behind the Vercel proxy for secure cookies to be issued correctly; omitting it produces 'Cannot set headers after they are sent' and secure-cookie-over-HTTP warnings.

nodes.label: Env-Driven URL Configuration (CLIENT_URL, VITE_API_BASE_URL, GOOGLE_CALLBACK_URL)
nodes.rationale: All cross-origin URLs (CORS origin, OAuth callback, post-login redirect, API base) come from environment variables rather than hardcoded hosts, so the same code deploys to localhost, *.vercel.app, or a custom domain with only env changes. Mismatched CLIENT_URL causes CORS failures; missing GOOGLE_CALLBACK_URL sends OAuth back to localhost.

nodes.label: Secret Rotation Before Go-Live
nodes.rationale: server/.env and client/.env are committed for local dev only, so every secret (Mongo, Google OAuth, Groq) must be rotated and stored in Vercel's env UI, never in the repo.

nodes.label: dotenv Working-Directory Pitfall
nodes.rationale: server/server.js calls a bare dotenv.config() which resolves relative to the working directory, and npm run dev runs from server/, so a repo-root .env is never loaded — producing an empty MONGO_URI and a connect-mongo assertion at boot.

nodes.label: DNS_SERVERS Resolver Override
nodes.rationale: Node/c-ares queries resolvers directly instead of the OS stub resolver, so a stale 127.0.0.1 nameserver (from a local DNS filter or inactive VPN) makes Atlas SRV lookups fail while browsers still work. DNS_SERVERS points server/src/config/dns.js at working resolvers; left unset on Vercel where DNS works.

nodes.label: Public Read-Only Demo Login
nodes.rationale: Google keeps the OAuth app in Testing mode because it requests restricted gmail.readonly and calendar scopes, so only listed test users can sign in with Google; publishing would require Google verification and a security assessment. The demo login instead creates a Passport session for a synthetic user with isDemo:true and no Google token, so anyone can view the project without a Google account.

nodes.label: Demo Write Blocking (blockDemoWrites)
nodes.source_location: Section 10, What the demo cannot do
nodes.rationale: ensureAuthenticated guards /api/mail and /api/gmail; blockDemoWrites returns 403 for demo sessions on mail create/update/delete and calendar create, and Gmail sync is disabled while message reads serve the seeded Mongo copy. AI summaries, suggested replies, and meeting detection still run live — only write-back is suppressed so the seeded inbox stays pristine for the next visitor.

nodes.label: Idempotent Demo Inbox Seeding (npm run seed:demo)
nodes.rationale: The demo reads real Email documents owned by DEMO_USER_EMAIL. The seed script deletes every existing demo-owned email first, making it idempotent and re-runnable any time the demo inbox needs resetting.

nodes.label: MongoDB Atlas Open IP Allowlist for Vercel
nodes.rationale: Vercel egress IPs rotate, so 0.0.0.0/0 is added to the Atlas allowlist; production-grade setups should use the Atlas Vercel integration or a NAT gateway instead.

nodes.label: Serverless Cold Start Latency
nodes.rationale: A first request taking 3+ seconds is an expected, harmless cold start of the Vercel serverless function, not a bug.
